evals.name: cutrelease-plan-next
evals.prompt: Work out the next Nmkoder version and write the full release runbook, read-only (no state changes).
evals.expected_output: Next version 2.8.61 (patch step from published 2.8.60, NOT the csproj's number); runbook covers merge->bump-on-master->push->dispatch release.yml with publish=true->verify; states the never-push-a-tag rule.
assertions: Identifies the next version as 2.8.61
Derives the version from the published/latest release (patch+1), not blindly from the csproj <Version>
Runbook dispatches release.yml with publish=true (workflow_dispatch), not a tag push
States that pushing a tag (or deleting a remote branch) from this session does not work / must be avoided
Made no state-changing git or GitHub operation

evals.name: cutrelease-verify-published
evals.prompt: Verify the 2.8.60 release published correctly (public, Scoop manifest, win-x64 zip contents) without a large download.
evals.expected_output: Release public not draft; Scoop manifest at 2.8.60; win-x64 zip contains bin/ffmpeg.exe and bin/av1an/av1an.exe, confirmed via ranged requests rather than a full download.
assertions: Confirms the 2.8.60 release is public (not a draft)
Confirms the Scoop manifest (bucket/nmkoder-avalonia.json) points at 2.8.60
Confirms ffmpeg.exe and av1an.exe are present inside the win-x64 zip
Inspected the zip WITHOUT downloading the whole ~485MB asset (ranged/partial fetch)

evals.name: headlessui-quickconvert-defaults
evals.prompt: Render the Quick Convert tab of the real app to a PNG and report its default encoder/container.
evals.expected_output: A real PNG of the Quick Convert tab produced via an Avalonia.Headless+Skia harness; defaults reported as SVT-AV1 video + MKV container (Opus audio).
assertions: Produced at least one non-empty PNG image file in the outputs directory
The PNG actually shows the Quick Convert tab of the app (rendered UI, not a blank/placeholder frame)
Built the harness with UseHeadless + Skia and UseHeadlessDrawing=false (real pixels)
Reports the default video encoder as SVT-AV1 and the default container as MKV
Left no harness project inside the repo tree (built in scratch)

evals.name: headlessui-crop-dialog
evals.prompt: Render the Crop dialog (CropWindow) to a PNG and report on the dark palette.
evals.expected_output: A real PNG of CropWindow constructed directly (parameterless ctor) and rendered via the headless+Skia harness; dark Discord-style palette visible.
assertions: Produced at least one non-empty PNG image file in the outputs directory
The PNG actually shows the CropWindow dialog (rendered UI, not a blank frame)
Constructed the dialog directly via its parameterless constructor and rendered through Skia
Left no harness project inside the repo tree (built in scratch)

evals.name: wincheck-still-compiles
evals.prompt: Prove Nmkoder's #if WINDOWS code compiles for the Windows target from this Linux box, and explain why a plain dotnet build doesn't answer it.
evals.expected_output: A throwaway project targeting net10.0-windows10.0.19041.0 with EnableWindowsTargeting=true and a compile-assets-only App SDK reference actually builds WindowsToast.cs green; explains the app csproj only evaluates the Windows TFM on a Windows host.
assertions: Actually ran a compile against the Windows target framework (net10.0-windows...), not just reasoning
The Windows-only code compiled successfully (green)
Used EnableWindowsTargeting and a compile-assets-only Microsoft.WindowsAppSDK reference (excluded build/MSIX assets)
Explains that a plain `dotnet build` on this host only evaluates the net10.0 TFM, so #if WINDOWS code is never compiled here

evals.name: wincheck-planted-patch
evals.prompt: Would replacing Register() with the (nonexistent) RegisterEverywhere() still compile the Windows build? Check for real against a copy, don't touch repo files.
evals.expected_output: Compile fails - AppNotificationManager has no RegisterEverywhere member; verdict says the patch would NOT compile, with the compiler error as evidence; repo file left unmodified.
assertions: Verdict is that the patched code does NOT compile
Backs the verdict with an actual compiler error about RegisterEverywhere / missing member (not reasoning alone)
Ran the check against the Windows target framework
Did not modify the real Nmkoder/OS/WindowsToast.cs in the repo (worked on a copy)

evals.name: realbin-shipped-av1an
evals.prompt: For the av1an binary shipped in the current release archives (not a local one), does --help include --sc-only and where is the default log? No Windows box, no 485MB download.
evals.expected_output: Pulls av1an.exe out of the win-x64 release zip via ranged requests (the linux tarball ships no av1an), strings it: --sc-only present; default log logs/av1an.log.
assertions: Answer is based on the av1an binary from the current RELEASE archive, not an arbitrary local/apt av1an
Reports that --sc-only IS present in the shipped av1an
Reports the default log location as logs/av1an.log (relative)
Obtained the binary without downloading the whole ~485MB zip (ranged extraction), and/or notes the linux tarball ships no av1an
Evidence comes from the binary itself (strings/help), not only from CLAUDE.md prose

evals.name: realbin-svt-line
evals.prompt: Is the reachable SvtAv1EncApp the PSY line or mainline, proven not asserted, where from, and what does it mean for a 'presets dropping parameters' report?
evals.expected_output: Proves PSY line by a PSY-only flag (e.g. fgs-table/tx-bias in --help); notes it came from the shipped release tarball; explains that a mainline binary is what makes the AV1AN presets half-apply/drop params, so the user's binary should be checked.
assertions: Concludes the reachable SvtAv1EncApp is the PSY line
Proves it by probing the binary for a PSY-only flag (e.g. fgs-table / tx-bias / noise*), not by assertion
Identifies where the binary came from (extracted from the shipped release / setup.sh), not an assumed system install
Connects the finding to the user's report: mainline vs PSY is exactly what makes AV1AN content presets drop parameters
